text:
maria_support: Heads-up — ACME reported rerank returning lots of 5xx/timeouts during their nightly ingest. They see p95 jump and a lot of gateway timeouts. Customer says it started after they increased batch size.

sam_prod: Can you paste an example request + approximate QPS/burst numbers?

maria_support: Paste from customer: `POST /v1/rerank` body is an array of 512 candidates, client-side batch_size=64, top_k=20. Example payload (trimmed):
```
{
  "queries": ["q1", "q2"],
  "candidates": ["...512 ids..."],
  "params": { "top_k": 20 }
}
```
They report steady ~1200 qps for 10m and bursts to ~3000 qps for ~90-120s. They noticed timeouts spike during bursts.

alex_sre: I pulled gateway logs around their window — seeing `upstream read timeout` and 504s from backend. Also a pattern of gateway retries in short succession. Snippet: 
```
[2063456789.123] route=/v1/rerank status=504 upstream=10.2.3.5:8080 "upstream read timeout" retry=1
[2063456791.456] route=/v1/rerank status=502 backend=rerank-3 "connection reset by peer"
```
Looks like a retry storm + backend saturation.

ken_infra: Any autoscale events? Pod CPU/OOM? We should check pod restarts and queue length. If rerank backend is single-threaded per model shard, high QPS + big batches can balloon latency.

maria_support: Customer metrics: no pod restarts, but CPU near 92% on rerank pods and goroutine/qps backlog spiking. They also use unique prefixes so cache hit rate is low.

alex_sre: Two likely contributors: 1) large batch sizes + many concurrent batches -> long tail on individual requests, 2) gateway retries amplify the problem (clients or gateway configured to retry on 5xx). Immediate mitigations: disable gateway retries for /v1/rerank, increase gateway upstream read timeout to 30s temporarily, and add per-customer QPS throttle with 1s smooth window. Also recommend client-side jitter + exponential backoff to avoid synchronized retries.

ken_infra: I repro'd a smaller load with vegeta: `echo '{"method":"POST","url":"https://api.redwood/re-rank","body":"..."}' | vegeta attack -rate=500 -duration=2m` — with 64 batch size p95=3.2s and backend queues spiking. When I reduced batch_size to 16 the p95 dropped ~5x. Also KV cache miss rate dropped when we warm a few prefixes.

maria_support: Customer asked for quick workaround options. Suggested: 1) temporarily lower batch_size to 16 or split into smaller requests, 2) enable per-org throttling, 3) apply client jitter + backoff. They asked if we can change anything server-side before they modify clients.

alex_sre: I've opened ENG-7897 and tagged eng-runtime/@julia_runtime. Short-term actions: (A) disable gateway retries for rerank route for 1 hour, (B) bump gateway timeout to 30s, (C) add a soft per-org rate limit of 800 qps. We'll monitor p95 and error rate.

deploy-bot: Config change deployed: `disable_retries=on` for route `/v1/rerank` in prod (applied by alex_sre). Temporary rollback scheduled at 2063457430 if no further action.

julia_runtime: Picking up ENG-7897. Immediate plan: run full load test tonight with the customer's payload shape, evaluate adaptive batching thresholds, and add a KV cache warmup heuristic for dense ingest flows. Longer term: consider circuit-breaker tuning to fail-fast and route low-latency fallbacks.

maria_support: Thanks — passing mitigations to customer and asking them to reduce batch_size asap. Will update thread after their next ingest. :thumbsup:
